Who Lakeshore is - operating profile to validate

AbarVa should begin with Lakeshore's corporate facts, portfolio shape, and strategy - not with a blank chat box.

Lakeshore is represented here as a diversified private holdings company with a parent sponsor, multiple operating platforms, portfolio-wide treasury exposure, and a practical mandate: make AI useful by improving cost, growth, risk, working capital, and execution discipline. The modeled operating mix intentionally resembles the public Chicago private-holdings archetype: supply chain and logistics, brand services, consumer products, and workplace convenience services. During the first 30 days, AbarVa would validate the revenue profile, company roster, countries, systems, vendors, banking estate, and board priorities with Lakeshore leadership.

Corpus is not set in stone

The corpus must be editable, governed, and local to Lakeshore's doctrine.

AbarVa should not pretend the first generated pattern is the truth forever. The right product stance is editorial control. Lakeshore's CFO, Treasurer, CIO, GC, and operating partners should be able to approve, refine, retire, or localize doctrine as the system learns what matters in their portfolio.

Approve or edit doctrine

Promote a pattern from generated draft to approved Lakeshore operating doctrine, with owner and vintage.

Localize by HoldCo

Capture Lakeshore-specific exceptions, bank-specific rules, PortCo system realities, and informal approval patterns.

Retire weak assumptions

Flag bad patterns, downgrade confidence, attach the evidence gap, or kill patterns that would mislead executives.

Corpus edit action

Change the decision owner from "CFO" to "Treasurer + CFO approval" when the pattern touches bank connectivity or intercompany lending.

Corpus evidence action

Attach a board pack, bank matrix, ERP feed audit, or implementation gate as the proof behind the pattern.

Corpus workflow action

Link a pattern to a Move phase or Source stage so the answer becomes an artifact, not just advice.

Corpus value action

Tie a pattern to forecast and realized savings so Tower can separate thesis from proof.

Plate 2 - Source Strategy: the Kyriba event begins with strategy, scope, readiness, and value guardrails.

Why Kyriba is the right wedge

Treasury modernization fails when the operating facts are discovered too late.

Kyriba is not just a software rollout. It depends on bank connectivity, ERP feed quality, entity hierarchy, historical cash data, adoption discipline, intercompany controls, and board-grade value proof. AbarVa turns those failure points into gates, artifacts, owners, and decisions before the rollout burns time.

The value of AbarVa is that it does not wait for a steering committee to discover the gaps in month four. It asks for the bank matrix, ERP feed evidence, entity map, cash history, control design, and owner decisions up front, then converts the weak spots into Source events, Move gates, and board-ready action.

Bank connectivity ERP feed quality Entity hierarchy Intercompany controls Covenant headroom BEC controls

Move 0 readiness gates: what AbarVa should force into the open

These are not checklist slogans. Each gate is a decision package with a named owner, evidence artifact, pass/fail rule, and failure mode. This is how AbarVa de-risks the rollout before Kyriba becomes an expensive implementation drag.

Gate 1

Bank inventory and connectivity

Checks: each bank, account, entity, currency, balance type, protocol, portal dependency, H2H/SWIFT/BAI2/MT940 path, timeline, and bank owner.

Artifact: bank connectivity matrix and sequencing plan.

Prevents: tail banks delaying the core cash-visibility rollout.
Gate 2

ERP, AP, AR, and GL feed quality

Checks: chart-of-accounts mapping, AP/AR extracts, cash-vs-GL variance, file cadence, exception queue, and reconciliation ownership.

Artifact: finance feed scorecard with remediation owners.

Prevents: Kyriba going live while reconciliation remains manual.
Gate 3

Entity and account hierarchy

Checks: HoldCo, PortCo, trust, family-office, lender, bank-account, intercompany, tax, and reporting hierarchy alignment.

Artifact: canonical treasury entity registry.

Prevents: wrong rollups, failed eliminations, and bad board reporting.
Gate 4

Historical cash reconstruction

Checks: 12-24 months of daily positions where available, missing banks, stale statements, currency gaps, and forecast-driver quality.

Artifact: Bronze/Silver historical cash data set.

Prevents: predictive forecasting becoming a weak demo with no training base.
Gate 5

Controls, adoption, and fraud posture

Checks: wire approval matrix, first-time payee callback, BEC controls, segregation of duties, role dashboards, and Excel-elimination plan.

Artifact: treasury controls and adoption playbook.

Prevents: users staying in bank portals and Excel after go-live.
Gate 6

Intercompany and covenant discipline

Checks: promissory notes, AFR-or-above rates, monthly true-up, IC journals, TTM EBITDA, leverage, FCCR, and covenant headroom.

Artifact: IC reconciliation and covenant forecast pack.

Prevents: audit/tax exposure and board surprise on covenant pressure.

Treasury doctrine AbarVa should know before it answers

Daily cash position

The Treasurer pre-walks position by 9am Central. More than 5% surprise requires same-day reconciliation.

Bank connectivity matrix

H2H, SWIFT, BAI2, MT940/MT942, portal-only banks, owners, and timeline risk must be known before Kyriba sequencing.

ERP and GL feed audit

Cash-vs-GL variance, AP/AR feed reliability, chart-of-accounts mapping, and exception workflow define the real rollout path.

Entity hierarchy

HoldCo, PortCo, trust, family-office, bank-account, and intercompany structure must be canonical before treasury automation.

Intercompany lending

Promissory notes, AFR-or-above rates, arms-length terms, monthly true-up, and tax/accounting review are not optional.

Covenant forecasting

TTM EBITDA, leverage, fixed-charge coverage, and interest coverage should be forecast at least 12 weeks ahead.

Payment controls

Wire approval matrices, first-time payee callback, dollar-threshold escalation, and BEC controls belong in the workflow.

Cash pooling and FX

Physical vs notional pooling, tax consequences, natural hedges, forwards, and ASC 815 reporting should be surfaced clearly.

Why a $500K / six-month investment is rational

The business case is not "buy AI." It is "turn portfolio complexity into signed decisions and measurable value."

AbarVa should justify the first six months by producing a small number of board-grade decisions with evidence, owners, artifacts, and value tracking. The target is not to claim every dollar on day one. The target is to build a governed value pipeline where finance can distinguish baseline, forecast, negotiated outcome, realized savings, and evidence gaps.

Decision standard

Public TMS buyer guidance indicates commercial treasury software plus implementation can range from hundreds of thousands into multi-million-dollar first-year programs depending on modules, bank connectivity, integrations, geographies, and services. AbarVa should calculate Lakeshore's real exposure from the Kyriba order form, SI SOW, bank matrix, and ERP integration plan, then show where failure avoidance, vendor leverage, and execution-cost reduction create 5-10x value potential.

Live product proof plates

Show the process flow one screen at a time.

Screenshots are useful when they show the buyer how the work moves through the product. The rule is one screen per proof plate: setup context, strategy, Move execution, Source decision, and Tower value proof.

Move: Kyriba rollout de-risk

The Move view keeps the program from becoming a loose advisory thread. It shows phase, owner, value-at-stake, artifacts, evidence, and next action.

Decision artifact

Move charter and gate checklist.

Evidence gap

Which bank, ERP, entity, or data item still needs proof.

Plate 3 - Move Detail: the rollout becomes owned work with phase, evidence, value, and next action.

Plate 4 - Source Decision: cropped to one readable page plate. The full long-scroll capture stays in the QA appendix.

Source: executive decision

The Source surface is where procurement, finance, and executive judgment meet. For Kyriba, it can show bank/SI selection, readiness issues, value guardrails, and the decision fork: move now on critical banks or expand scope once evidence improves.

Decision discipline

Forecast value should stay separate from realized value. AbarVa should show the evidence, owner, approval state, and next artifact required before any claim becomes finance-attested.

Value pipeline: proof before realized savings

The right buyer story is not "$0 realized value." It is a controlled value pipeline: opportunities are visible, forecast value is tracked, and realized savings only count after baseline evidence, intervention record, negotiated outcome, and finance attestation.

Baseline

What finance accepts as current truth.

Forecast

What the Move expects to improve.

Realized

What is proven after action.

Gap

What still blocks the claim.

Six-month engagement shape

Six months should build the intelligence layer, prove finance/treasury success, and create a reusable AI execution engine.

Month 1

Stand up the Lakeshore context layer: enterprise profile, org, systems, CMDB, vendors, contracts, banking, KPIs, risks, and evidence.

Month 2

Build the editable corpus: treasury, finance, governance, vendor, IT, risk, and operating-company doctrine with approval workflow.

Month 3

Run Kyriba / treasury readiness gates and produce the CFO/Treasurer evidence pack for bank, ERP, entity, cash, control, and IC gaps.

Month 4

Launch Source value events: bank rationalization, SI readiness, audit/advisory leverage, vendor overlap, and renewal optimization.

Month 5

Move 3-5 opportunities through execution with artifacts, owners, approval state, and finance-reviewed value logic.

Month 6

Publish the board-ready AI Success Platform pack: value ledger, corpus coverage, operating model, roadmap, and renewal case.

Six-month success standard

The program should earn renewal by showing 5-10x value potential with finance-defensible proof.

The renewal case should not be a polished demo. It should be a board-grade evidence package showing what context was loaded, what corpus doctrine was approved, which treasury and sourcing risks were avoided, which vendor or implementation costs were optimized, and which AI use cases can now be executed at lower cost and higher control.

Context and corpus proof

Coverage of Lakeshore entities, systems, vendors, contracts, banking, KPIs, risks, artifacts, and approved doctrine.

Finance / treasury proof

Kyriba readiness gates, failure-cost avoidance, bank/ERP/entity gaps, IC/covenant controls, and CFO-owned decisions.

ROI proof

5-10x value potential shown through Source pipeline, vendor optimization, execution-cost reduction, and finance-attested value ledger.

Claim discipline: screenshots are product proof from the Lakeshore demo packet; planning baselines should be validated with Lakeshore before being treated as client-approved facts; generated artifacts remain drafts until reviewed; forecast value is not realized value.
